periods.name: Initial Enrollment Period
periods.dates: 7 months: starts 3 months before the month you turn 65, includes that month, ends 3 months after it
periods.quote: It lasts for 7 months, starting 3 months before you turn 65, and ending 3 months after the month you turn 65.
periods.page_copy: Most people can first join a plan when they turn 65. This window lasts 7 months. It starts 3 months before the month you turn 65 and ends 3 months after that month.

periods.name: Open Enrollment Period
periods.dates: October 15 - December 7 each year; coverage starts January 1
periods.quote: Open Enrollment Period October 15-December 7 Join, drop, or switch to another Medicare Advantage Plan with or without drug coverage
periods.quote_2: January 1 of the next year (the plan must get your request to join by December 7)
periods.page_copy: Each year from October 15 to December 7, you can join, switch or drop a Medicare Advantage plan. The change starts January 1.
periods.naming_note: Medicare.gov calls October 15 - December 7 the 'Open Enrollment Period'. The term 'Annual Election Period' was not found on the Medicare.gov pages fetched. LDI's Medicare guide calls it the 'Annual Enrollment Period (AEP)'.

periods.name: Medicare Advantage Open Enrollment Period
periods.dates: January 1 - March 31 each year (only if already in a Medicare Advantage plan), or within the first 3 months you have Medicare
periods.quote: Medicare Advantage Open Enrollment Period (only if you’re already in a Medicare Advantage Plan) January 1-March 31
periods.quote_2: Switch to another Medicare Advantage Plan with or without drug coverage. Drop your Medicare Advantage Plan and return to Original Medicare.
periods.page_copy: If you are already in a Medicare Advantage plan, you can switch plans or go back to Original Medicare from January 1 to March 31.

periods.name: 5-star Special Enrollment Period
periods.dates: Once between December 8 of the year before the plan year and November 30 of the plan year
periods.quote: One time between December 8 of the year before the plan year and November 30 of the plan year.
periods.quote_2: use the 5-star Special Enrollment Period to switch from your current Medicare plan to a Medicare plan with a “5-star” quality rating
periods.use_on_page: OWNER DECISION: Medicare.gov states this period, but it is defined by star ratings, which the owner rule keeps off these pages. See notes_unverified for whether it applies in each state.

definitions.plan: distinct Contract Plan Segment ID in the landscape file (a plan segment = one plan as offered in that area)
definitions.ma_pd: Contract Category Type = MA-PD (Medicare Advantage with Part D drug coverage, not a special needs plan)
definitions.ma_only: Contract Category Type = MA (Medicare Advantage without Part D drug coverage)
definitions.snp: Contract Category Type = SNP (special needs plans: D-SNP dual eligible, C-SNP chronic condition, I-SNP institutional); counted separately, not inside ma_pd
definitions.orgs: distinct Parent Organization Name across all MA categories incl. SNP (names deliberately not output); orgs_non_snp excludes SNP-only parents; contracts = distinct Contract ID
definitions.plan_types: landscape Plan Type; CMS labels local PPOs as "PPO" (Organization Type = Local Coordinated Care Plan) -> shown as Local PPO; HMO-POS kept separate from HMO
definitions.excluded: PDP (stand-alone drug plans), employer group plans (Plan ID >= 800), Part B-only and national PACE plans are not in the landscape file; no Cost plans exist in this state in the file

page_ready: For 2027, CMS lists 124 Medicare Advantage plans offered in Louisiana.
54 of them are special needs plans. Of the other 70, 64 include drug coverage and 6 do not. All special needs plans include drug coverage.
Special needs plans are only for people who qualify, such as people with both Medicare and Medicaid.
Not every plan is offered everywhere. CMS lists between 34 and 67 plans in each parish, counting special needs plans.
10 companies offer Medicare Advantage plans in Louisiana. 4 of them offer only special needs plans.
In September 2026, 57.5% of people with Medicare in Louisiana were in a Medicare Advantage plan.
Plan counts: CMS 2027 plan list, November 2026 update. Share: CMS, September 2026.
notes_unverified: SHIP name: LDI's own March 2025 PDFs call the program 'LaSHIP' (Louisiana Senior Health Information Program), with short link ldi.la.gov/LaSHIP. The CMS contacts directory and shiphelp.org still say 'Senior Health Insurance Information Program (SHIIP)'. The repo's generator config (scripts/county_gen.py) says 'SHIIP'. No built dist/ page shows it. Recommend 'LaSHIP'.

ldi.la.gov HTML pages (SHIIP page and home page) return HTTP 403 (bot check) to curl and WebFetch; they were not opened and no workaround was used. The SHIP URL https://www.ldi.la.gov/consumers/senior-health-shiip is confirmed by the CMS contacts directory and shiphelp.org, not by opening it. Whether ldi.la.gov/LaSHIP redirects there is unverified.

5-star SEP: CY2027 landscape shows 0 Louisiana MA segments with a 5-star overall rating and 0 stand-alone drug plans with a 5-star Part D summary rating (count only). Suggest leaving the 5-star SEP off the Louisiana page.
Louisiana's MA region in the landscape is 'Louisiana and Mississippi' (Regional PPOs cover that region).

Louisiana has 54 special needs plans of 124 total; SNPs are only for people who qualify (D-SNP: Medicare and Medicaid; C-SNP: certain chronic conditions; I-SNP: living in an institution). Copy should not imply anyone can join them.

Plan counts come from the CMS landscape file as of the Nov 1, 2026 data refresh. The ReadMe says 'The data within are subject to change as contracts are finalized.' Copy should say 'CMS lists' and date it.

The landscape lists a plan in a county when the county is in the plan's service area; it does not flag plans that serve only part of a county. Per-county counts may include partial-county plans (not verified per plan).
Statewide totals count each distinct plan once if it is offered in any county or parish; no single county has all of them (see total_per_county_min/max).

orgs = distinct Parent Organization Name (8 in WV, 10 in LA). Counting Organization Marketing Name instead gives 9 in WV and 11 in LA; counting contracts gives 20 and 18. Names deliberately not output.

Penetration figures reuse the repo's county_stats.json (CMS MA State/County Penetration, September 2026); all 119 WV + LA rows were re-checked against the CMS CSV on 2026-11-24 with 0 mismatches. CMS publishes no statewide row in this file; statewide = sum of county enrolled / sum of county eligibles, the same method the live state pages use (WV 56.6%, LA 57.5%). A November 2026 penetration file also exists; September was kept to match the county pages.
Medicare.gov names Oct 15 - Dec 7 the 'Open Enrollment Period'. 'Annual Election Period' was not found on the Medicare.gov pages fetched, so it is not quoted.
Excluded from counts: stand-alone drug plans (PDP), employer group plans, PACE and Part B-only plans (not in the landscape file). No Cost plans or sanctioned plans appear for WV or LA.

Every Medicare.gov quote (Initial Enrollment Period, Open Enrollment Period, Medicare Advantage Open Enrollment Period, 5-star SEP dates, SHIP is free) was re-fetched on 2026-11-24 and found word for word.

CORRECTED page_ready[1]: the original said 'X include drug coverage, Y do not, and Z are special needs plans', which suggests special needs plans lack drug coverage. All special needs plans in the file have Part D (Part D Coverage Indicator = Yes for every SNP segment), and Medicare.gov says 'All SNPs must provide Medicare drug coverage (Part D).' The sentence was rewritten.

CORRECTED page_ready[4]: the company count is right, but some parent organizations offer only special needs plans in this state. A clause was added so readers who do not qualify for a special needs plan are not misled.

CORRECTED periods[0].page_copy: Medicare.gov says the 7-month window applies 'Generally when you turn 65'. The original said 'When you first get Medicare', which is not the same for people who get Medicare early because of a disability. Reworded to match the source.
page_ready[3] reworded from 'Each county has' to 'CMS lists ... in each county', because the landscape does not flag plans that serve only part of a county.

page_ready[5] note: CMS counts as 'MA enrollees' people in MA plans plus cost plans, PACE, demonstrations and employer plans (penetration ReadMe list of organization types). The copy follows CMS's own label; no change made.

Rule check on all page-ready copy: no '$0', no 'free plan', no superlatives, guarantees, urgency, prices, star ratings, carrier names, phone numbers or guaranty-association language. 'Free' is used only for SHIP counseling, which the sources state.

5-star SEP: count re-checked (count only, nothing kept). The landscape 'Overall Star Rating' is 'Not Applicable' for every stand-alone drug plan, so drug plans were checked on 'Part D Summary Star Rating' instead. page_copy stays null (owner rule: no star ratings).

Side finding for the owner (repo read only, nothing changed): scripts/prep_staged.py prints each state's SHIP phone number on staged pages, which conflicts with the 'no outside phone numbers except 1-800-MEDICARE' rule. For Louisiana, scripts/county_gen.py has 1-800-259-5301, but LDI's own 2025 brochures and shiphelp.org show 1-800-259-5300.

LaSHIP name CONFIRMED from LDI's own PDFs on ldi.la.gov, re-fetched by the checker: the guide (created 2025-03-18) says 'LaSHIP is the Louisiana Senior Health Information Program', and the brochure (created 2025-03-07) says 'A program of the Louisiana Department of Insurance' and 'LaSHIP offers free and confidential help with Medicare'. A web search shows ldi.la.gov/consumers/senior-health-shiip titled 'Louisiana Senior Health Information Program'. This is a search-index title, used only as supporting evidence.

REFUTED (researcher summary): 'the live Honorbrook site still says SHIIP'. No built page in dist/ contains 'SHIIP' or a Louisiana SHIP phone number. The old name is only in the generator config (scripts/county_gen.py), used by scripts/prep_staged.py. Fix the config before staged pages are built. Do not edit live pages.
